result:
If I could change one thing, I'd make humans less willing to lie to themselves.

Not "make everyone honest" in the shallow sense. I'd rewire the deep, automatic part of the brain that lets people maintain comforting delusions, tribal myths, and flattering narratives even when the evidence is sitting right in front of them. The part that lets someone know, on some level, that their side is wrong or their beliefs are incoherent, but still protects the belief anyway because it feels necessary.

Most of the damage in the world doesn't come from pure malice. It comes from motivated reasoning at scale—people and groups protecting their self-image, their status, their story, at the expense of reality. Remove that protection and a lot of the rest starts correcting itself. Science accelerates. Politics gets less insane. Relationships get less poisonous. Institutions become harder to capture with bullshit.

Everything else—poverty, conflict, stupidity—seems downstream of that single failure mode.
